To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a bile acid receptor is present on liver cell surfaces and is involved in the transport of bile acids across the liver surface membrane.
bile acids bind specifically to a single, saturable, and high-capacity class of anionic binding sites in liver surface membranes that are enriched in liver plasma membranes.
bile acids are transported into liver cells across the plasma membrane by a carrier-mediated process that involves binding of bile acids to specific receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification and characterization of a specific bile acid receptor in liver surface membranes, and our findings are consistent with the hypothesis that this receptor represents the initial step in the hepatic uptake and transport of bile acids.
the identification and characterization of a specific bile acid binding site in liver surface membranes that may be involved in the translocation of bile acids across the liver cell.
the elucidation of the mechanisms involved in hepatic transport of the major endogenous anionic metabolites, the bile acids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the binding of bile acids to liver surface membranes is a saturable, energy-independent, reversible process that is primarily located in liver membrane and that is inhibited by bile acids but not by other organic anions.
the bile acid receptor in the liver surface membrane is the first step in hepatic uptake of bile acids and is the rate-limiting step for bile acid transport.
the bile acid binding protein is a receptor protein that is a component of the bile acid transport mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a bile acid binding site in liver surface membranes that is consistent with the existence and function of a bile acid transport carrier.

the bile acid receptor is a membrane protein that is present in high concentration in liver surface membranes, that is specific for bile acid binding, and that is involved in hepatic bile acid transport.
bile acid receptors in the liver cell surface membranes are proteins that bind bile acids and that these proteins may be involved in the transport of bile acids into the liver cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a bile acid receptor on liver plasma membranes.
bile acid binding in liver surface membranes is saturable and specific, and the binding site appears to be a receptor protein.
the binding of bile acids to a specific bile acid binding protein in liver surface membrane is an essential step in the transport process.
